title: Duress Device Renders
summary: A comprehensive rendered asset library for all Duress devices and accessories, including all UI screen variations. A custom Photoshop plugin was developed to reduce batch export times.

meta.Deliverables: Full rendered asset library, all UI screen variations, custom Photoshop UXP plugin

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.heading: One library, every device, every angle.
paras: I developed a streamlined workflow to create a comprehensive library of rendered assets for every Duress device and accessory. Starting with 3D modeling in Blender and rendering in Keyshot, I implemented consistent angles, file naming, and a custom Photoshop plugin to batch-generate all screen variations across artboards.

blocks.label: 3D modelling & rendering
blocks.heading: Model in Blender, light in KeyShot.
paras: 3D modelling started in Blender with some devices needing topology refining. These were then put into Keyshot and set up with lighting, materials and cameras for batch rendering.

blocks.label: Angles & naming
blocks.heading: Forty-five degrees at a time.
paras: Angles were sorted in 45 degree increments for an expansive library of render assets. Naming conventions were clear, marked with the device color, angle and screen content (e.g. eagle-render-emergency-black-45.png).

blocks.label: Screen UI & batch exporting
blocks.heading: A plugin to do the boring part.
paras: Screens were then added as a linked Photoshop file and organised in artboards. I then developed a Photoshop UXP plugin to do the batch exporting for every screen in the linked file for all artboards in the main file.
